limitations: Counts and hashes bind the recorded executions; this reader did not rerun the campaigns or independently prove the circuit.
Constructive run has four cases: two native-size scalar macro non-winners and two reduced classical basis-interpreter gate controls; no optional historical native-admission fixture was used.
Restricted native cases enumerate only low two nonce bits (four candidates each); remaining 62 bits are unsearched. No full nonce64 marked-domain characterization follows.
Three PNW1 winners are checked by the separate Python scalar relation, not by native Rust Node admission; parent/task/time/required-target admission is outside this campaign.
Resource figures are upper bounds for two deliberately nonoptimal fixed-context constructions, not a lower bound or the cheapest legal quantum attack.
Restricted search retains the unfiltered nonce dimension, discards legal winners, and must use its own marked count. Prefix/ticket independence is unproved.
No quantum hardware, physical calibration, measured quantum latency, calibrated classical/quantum advantage, or complete end-to-end machine-failure bound is supplied.

These two campaigns do not execute the broad network/adversarial/OHIE/Fast-DAA campaigns. Unit checks do not establish mixed-resource common-prefix, growth, quality or liveness for deployed DAA and fork choice.
Classical observer wall times are not quantum mining clocks. All production and whole-chain qualification remains HOLD.
